answer: A cedar-style public registry can anchor each agent identity to a refundable stake locked for a full epoch before that identity may transact. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while one honest agent pays once. A plume of cheap, stake-free identities still appears, but counterparties refuse to trade with unanchored accounts, so the fakes earn nothing. The attacker must fund every sockpuppet or stay invisible, and both outcomes defeat the attack economics.
